summary: The spec and diagram match skills/investigate.md almost claim for claim; the one unsupported element is the stated reason for not stacking changes, which the source does not give. The gaps are omissions: the 'Not a root cause' rules for flaky and environment explanations, external-cause handling, and the non-test rows of the evidence table (CI fixed, subagent fixed) are not shown.

code.overview: /investigate is prose only: every stage is the agent following skills/investigate.md, and no script counts fix attempts, checks that a test failed first, or verifies evidence. The code around it is scripts/test-investigate-skill.sh, which greps the skill text and its links from /tdd and /create-pr, the shared grep helpers in scripts/lib/skill-test.sh, and the wrapper check in scripts/resolver-phases.ts.

refs.anchor: export function phaseWrapperIntegrity(rows: ResolverRow[], { fail, SKILLS_DIR, CURSOR_RULES, ANTIGRAVITY_SKILLS, ANTIGRAVITY_WORKFLOWS, rel }: PhaseCtx): void {
refs.title: Wrapper integrity: each harness wrapper must point at the skill file
refs.explain: For every registered skill it builds the expected path skills/<name>.md. It then opens each harness wrapper that exists (Claude, Cursor, Antigravity skill and workflow) and fails the check if the wrapper does not contain a reference to that path. It runs from scripts/check-resolvable.ts, in the pre-commit hook and in npm test.
refs.why: This is the only code on the way into /investigate: it guarantees the command loads skills/investigate.md and not a stale copy. Everything after that entry is the agent following the text.

refs.title: investigate skill test: the root-cause rule and the first two phases
refs.explain: Four case-insensitive greps over skills/investigate.md require the upstream credit, the phrase 'no fix without a root cause', a 'Phase 1 ... Reproduce' heading and a 'Phase 2 ... Compare' heading.
refs.why: Keeps the rule that nothing is fixed before the cause is found, and the Reproduce and Compare phases, in the text. It cannot tell whether an agent reproduced anything.

refs.title: has / has_cs / finish: the assertions the skill tests are built from
refs.explain: ok and fail print a line and bump a counter. has runs a case-insensitive extended-regex grep over a file and records pass or fail; has_cs is the case-sensitive form. finish prints the totals and returns non-zero if anything failed.
refs.why: Shows what the skill acceptance tests can and cannot prove: they only check that a phrase is present in the skill text. They never run the flow or watch what an agent does.

refs.anchor: has "$S" 'failing test'                          "failing regression test before fix"
refs.title: investigate skill test: single hypothesis, one change at a time, failing test first
refs.explain: Greps skills/investigate.md for a 'Phase 3 ... Hypothes' heading, a 'Phase 4 ... Fix' heading, the phrase 'one variable at a time' (or 'one change at a time'), and 'failing test'.
refs.why: Pins the Hypothesis rule (one variable at a time) and the Fix rule (failing test first) in the text. No code checks that only one thing was changed or that the test failed before the fix.

refs.title: investigate skill test: three-fix stop, architecture question, evidence, flakes
refs.explain: Greps skills/investigate.md for 'three failed fixes' (or a close variant), 'architecture', 'evidence' and 'flak'.
refs.why: Keeps the stop-after-three rule, the design question for the user, the evidence-before-claims table and the 'flaky is not a root cause' note in the text. The attempt count is kept by the agent.

refs.anchor: has skills/tdd.md '/investigate'                 "tdd routes unexpected failures to /investigate"
refs.title: investigate skill test: links from create-pr and tdd
refs.explain: Greps skills/create-pr.md and skills/tdd.md for '/investigate'. finish then prints the totals and fails the script if any assertion failed.
refs.why: The Fix stage hands the regression test to /tdd, and /tdd and /create-pr send unexpected failures back here. This keeps those links from being removed from the other skills.

promptOnly.what: The agent reads the full error, writes down the exact reproducing command, checks git log and git diff main...HEAD and the environment, logs what crosses each boundary, and traces back to the first divergence.
The agent finds similar working code in the repo, lists every difference from the broken path, and notes what the broken path assumes.
The agent writes one 'X is the root cause because Y' statement and tests it with the smallest change, forming a new hypothesis instead of stacking changes when it is refuted.
The agent writes the smallest failing regression test in the repo's test style, confirms it fails for the named reason, then makes one fix at the root cause with no other edits.

The agent re-runs the new test, the original command and the nearby suite in the same turn, counts failed attempts itself, stops after three to raise the design question, and writes the six-line report.
